REVIEW:
# Review: Team Pricing Tier Launch Plan

The memo is well built. It leads with a clear recommendation, the timeline reasoning is easy to follow, and the arithmetic mostly checks out. The main problems are one internal contradiction that undercuts a headline finding, a few dependencies that aren't stated, and some loose ends.

## Arithmetic check

| Claim | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ~4.5 weeks before Dec 18 freeze | Nov 16 to Dec 18 = 32 days ≈ 4.6 wks | ✅ |
| Remaining 5.5 wks ends ~Feb 11 | Jan 4 + 38.5 days ≈ Feb 11 | ✅ |
| Jan 31 launch cuts ~1.5 wks | Jan 4 to Jan 31 ≈ 3.9 wks vs. 5.5 needed | ✅ (~1.6) |
| Free → Team +$2.6M | 4,533 × 4 × $12 × 12 = $2.61M | ✅ |
| Business → Team −$1.3M | 1,150 × 12 × $8 × 12 = $1.32M | ✅ |
| Net ≈ 9%, goal = $3.6M | Both imply a ~$14.4M base | ✅ consistent |
| Chat −$1.2M | 5,650 × $18 × 12 = $1.22M | ✅ |
| 37.5% of $48 | $18 / $48 | ✅ |

## Substantive issues

**1. "Team adds at most about a third" contradicts Condition 1.**
The one-third figure assumes the full −$1.3M Business loss. Condition 1 says the fence "avoids most of the $1.3M loss." If it does, net ARR moves toward $2.6M, which is about 70% of the goal, not a third.

The memo can't claim both. I suggest stating a range instead: about $1.3M unfenced, up to about $2.6M fenced. This also strengthens the case for the fence.

**2. The chat cost line uses the unfenced account count.**
The ~5,650 accounts include the 1,150 Business downgrades. With the fence, the count is closer to 4,500. Also, downgraders presumably already cost something to support on Business, so the incremental cost is lower still. The "barely contributes margin" finding is directionally right but overstated as written.

**3. The new billing platform dependency is unclear.**
The plan asks to approve the build "on the new billing platform" starting Nov 16, while the migration apparently completes around March 31. The memo should state that the platform is available to build against now. It should also explain what happens between build completion (~Feb 11) and launch (Apr 13): integration testing, or idle time.

The memo also notes that the 10-week estimate is unconfirmed for the new platform, yet asks leadership to commit to April 13. Either get the estimate confirmed before Nov 16 or present April 13 as a target pending that confirmation.

**4. The waitlist price lock works against the memo's own caution.**
The memo argues against launching when pricing can't be corrected. But a price lock commits to $12 two months before any real data comes in. I'd specify the lock's terms (duration, scope) or offer a launch discount instead.

**5. The announcement could undermine the fence.**
A public Feb 10 announcement will reach Business customers two months before launch. The plan needs messaging and Sales guidance for Business customers who ask about Team. Otherwise the "do not present at renewal" rule leaks before day one.

**6. The Sales timeline is tight.**
The comp change is due Feb 1 but must be announced before Feb 10. That leaves about a week for sign-off and rollout. Consider pulling the deadline to mid-January.

## Clarity and gaps

- **Condition 2 is vaguer in the summary than in the body.** The summary says "well below $18"; the body says "at or below $8." Use $8 in both places.
- **Inputs aren't sourced.** Cite where the 34%, 23%, and ⅓ figures come from. The ⅓ factor in particular is unexplained. Also note the 12-user / $8-gap assumptions for Business accounts.
- **There is no 2027 in-year estimate.** The memo says 2027 will be lower "because of the April start and gradual ramp" but gives no number. A rough figure would help the VP weigh the 25% goal.
- **The compliance point may double count.** If the 23% downgrade rate already excludes compliance-sensitive accounts, the 9% doesn't reduce exposure further. Clarify.
- **Formatting:** there is a stray empty `##` heading at the end of the document.

## Bottom line

The recommendation is sound, and the timeline case against Q1 is convincing. Fix the contradiction in item 1 and clarify the billing platform dependency in item 3 before this goes to the VP. Those are the two places where a careful reader will push back.
